messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE FIRED — capacity_exhaustion on runtime-queue-prod (us-west-2)
incident-bot: alert_id=capx-21478 severity=high queue_backlog=187k avg_latency=2.6s token_rate=~420/s
pd-bot: PagerDuty: Triggered -> service: runtime-queue-prod, urgency: high. Incident key: PD-INC-7892

maria (oncall): Acked in PD. I'm taking this. Looking at metrics now.

aj: on my way. any customer-facing errors?

maria (oncall): Dashboard shows consumer queue length spike after a burst at 03:12 UTC. Throughput hasn't scaled up; autoscaler not adding pods.

leo: seeing controller logs: `scale-loop skipped: recent_scale=30s` but desired_replicas keeps maxing out at 12. HPA events show "failed to reconcile: resource quota"
sam: resource-quota? which namespace?

leo: runtime-prod-gpu namespace. quota shows pods=12/12. Looks like quota cap hit from a leftover batch job.
maria (oncall): oof. that explains why autoscaler couldn't add capacity. Who owns that batch?

sam: `batch-etl-2026` owner is dataeng. pinging @customer-ops to confirm if that job should be killed.

customer-ops: Confirmed — that ETL job started unexpectedly due to a bad cron. We can stop it.

aj: while we stop it, we should manually scale down the ETL job or delete the job pods to free quota. I'm preparing kubectl commands.
maria (oncall): Good plan. Also switch routing fallback to lower-capacity variant to avoid tail latency for critical customers. Can someone trigger fallback?

leo: Deleting ETL pods now: `kubectl delete pods -l job=batch-etl-2026 -n runtime-prod-gpu`

leo: pods terminating. freeing up 5 pod slots.

eng-sre: Noted. Also bumping cluster quota would be possible but not safe mid-incident. Manual remediation first.

maria (oncall): Watching autoscaler events… it retried a scale at 03:18:12 and failed; new attempt at 03:19:01 appears to have succeeded, desired_replicas=18 -> current_replicas=18. Good.

incident-bot: capacity_exhaustion alert resolved (queue_backlog dropped to 12k). Monitoring for regression for 20m.

aj: rerouting change applied: critical-route -> runtime-variant-lowcost with degraded QoS for 8 customers (not ideal but reduces tail latency).

customer-ops: We saw 503 spike for ~7 minutes for a subset of users (percent impacted ~4%). Notifying affected customers per SLA.

maria (oncall): Timeline draft: 03:12 UTC sudden ETL cron -> pods consumed namespace quota -> autoscaler attempted scale but blocked by quota -> queue backlog grew to 187k -> 03:16 PD page fired -> 03:17 ETL pods deleted -> 03:19 autoscaler succeeded -> 03:21 backlog down to 12k.

sam: Root cause looks like an unintended cron plus missing guard on cluster quota usage by batch jobs.

leo: Filed a short-term post-incident mitigation: add quota alerting for batch-job owner and add runbook step to check namespace quota before scaling attempt.

maria (oncall): I'll hand off to night oncall in 25m. I'll also create the incident writeup and link metrics + kube events. Any follow-ups?

aj: Add a safety check to the autoscaler: if quota==max then emit a distinct alert so PD paging goes to batch-owners first.

customer-ops: Thanks team. We'll proceed with customer comms and follow-ups.

pd-bot: PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by maria (oncall). Escalation suspended.

incident-bot: Monitoring window started (20m). If backlog increases >20k again, page oncall.

maria (oncall): marking this thread as incident-ref: INC-21478-capacity-spiral. I'll post the notes shortly and tag eng-sre for a postmortem. :white_check_mark:
